q: A bakery owner signs a one-year lease for a storefront. Which element makes this agreement a legally binding contract?
r: An offer, acceptance and something of value exchanged by both parties
These elements form a valid contract.
w: A handshake and a friendly conversation between the two parties
Informal talk alone may not bind either side.
A verbal promise made in front of customers at the store
A promise without the required elements is weak.
A signature from only the landlord, without the owner agreeing
Both sides must agree.

q: What is the purpose of a trademark for a business?
r: To protect a name, logo or slogan that identifies its products
It stops others from using a confusing mark.
w: To guarantee that every product sold will make a profit
A mark does not ensure profit.
To give the government control over the company's prices
A trademark does not set prices.
To protect a new invention from being copied for 20 years
That describes a patent.

q: A song used in a store's online ad was written by a famous artist. What should the store get before using it?
r: Permission or a license from the copyright owner
Using protected work requires permission.
w: A receipt showing the song was purchased as a download
A personal purchase does not allow commercial use.
A note from a customer saying they like the song
Customer approval is not a license.
Nothing, because songs on the radio are free for business use
Public airplay does not remove copyright.

q: A customer slips on a wet floor with no warning sign and is injured. Which legal concept is most likely involved?
r: Negligence, a failure to use reasonable care
The store may have failed to prevent harm.
w: Fraud, a deliberate deception to gain money
No deliberate deception is described.
Libel, a false written statement that harms reputation
No false statement was made.
Bankruptcy, a legal process for businesses that cannot pay debts
This is unrelated to the injury.

q: What does a warranty on a product do?
r: Promises that the product will work or meet certain standards
It gives the buyer remedies if the promise fails.
w: Guarantees that the price will never go up
A warranty does not cover price changes.
Requires the buyer to return the product within one hour
That is a return rule.
Lets the seller change the product after the sale
A warranty protects the buyer.

q: Which type of business ownership gives owners limited personal liability for business debts?
r: A corporation or limited liability company
Owners risk only what they invested.
w: A sole proprietorship run by one person
The owner is personally responsible.
A general partnership between two friends
Partners share personal liability.
A business with no legal registration
Without protection, owners are exposed.

q: An employer pays a 16-year-old worker less than the minimum wage and schedules a 14-hour shift on a school night. Which laws are most likely being broken?
r: Wage and child labor laws
These laws set pay and limits on young workers.
w: Copyright and trademark laws
These protect creative works and brands.
Antitrust and merger laws
These govern competition between firms.
Zoning and building laws
These govern land use and construction.

q: What is the role of an agent in business law?
r: A person authorized to act on behalf of another, the principal
The principal can be bound by the agent's actions.
w: A person who inspects a business for tax errors
That describes an auditor.
A person who buys goods only for personal use
That describes a consumer.
A person who lends money to businesses
That describes a lender.

q: Why do businesses use written contracts instead of relying only on spoken agreements?
r: A written record shows the agreed terms and reduces disputes
Clear terms are easier to prove.
w: Spoken agreements are always illegal in business
Many spoken agreements are valid but hard to prove.
Written contracts remove the need to follow the terms
Terms must still be followed.
Written contracts guarantee that no one will ever disagree
They reduce, but do not end, disputes.

q: A company imports electronics and fails to follow customs rules at the border. What is the most likely result?
r: Shipments may be delayed, seized or fined
Customs rules are enforced at the border.
w: The shipment moves faster because it skips inspection
Ignoring rules triggers more review.
The company earns a government subsidy
Violations do not create subsidies.
The company becomes exempt from future import laws
Violations do not create exemptions.

q: What does the term 'liability' mean for a business?
r: A legal responsibility, often for debts or harm caused
Liability can create obligations to pay.
w: The total revenue a business earns in a year
That is revenue.
The value of a company's trademarks
That describes intangible assets.
The number of employees a company must hire
That is a staffing matter.

q: A supplier promises delivery by Friday in a signed contract but ships a week late. What is this called?
r: A breach of contract
One party failed to perform as promised.
w: A merger between two companies
A merger combines firms.
A tariff on imported goods
A tariff is a tax.
A patent infringement
That involves an invention.

q: Which agency enforces rules that protect consumers from deceptive advertising in the United States?
r: The Federal Trade Commission
It handles unfair or deceptive practices.
w: The Federal Reserve
It manages monetary policy.
The Securities and Exchange Commission
It regulates securities markets.
The Internal Revenue Service
It collects federal taxes.

q: What is the main purpose of environmental regulations for businesses?
r: To limit pollution and protect natural resources
Companies must meet environmental standards.
w: To increase the prices of all products
Regulations do not set prices directly.
To protect companies from competition
Their aim is environmental protection.
To help businesses avoid paying taxes
They do not exempt firms from taxes.

q: Two competing firms secretly agree to set the same high prices. Which law does this most likely violate?
r: Antitrust law against price fixing
Competitors may not agree on prices.
w: Copyright law protecting written works
Price agreements do not involve copyrights.
Child labor law limiting teen work
The situation is unrelated to hiring.
Zoning law controlling land use
Zoning does not govern pricing.

q: Which channel is best for sharing a detailed, formal policy change with all employees?
r: A written memo or email with clear details
Written messages create a record.
w: A quick hallway comment to a few workers
Not everyone would get the details.
A text message with no explanation
It lacks needed detail.
A rumor passed from coworker to coworker
Rumors distort the message.

q: What is the first step in writing a clear business email?
r: Decide the purpose and who the reader is
Purpose and audience guide the message.
w: Add as many attachments as possible
More attachments do not add clarity.
Write in all capital letters for emphasis
That seems like shouting.
Include every detail from the past year
Too much detail hides the point.

q: A manager's words say 'I'm open to ideas' but she frowns and crosses her arms. What does this show?
r: Her nonverbal cues may contradict her message
Body language can undermine words.
w: She has a strong written communication style
The scenario describes body language.
She is using the most effective channel
Contradiction weakens the message.
She is following a company policy on tone
No policy is mentioned.

q: Why is it useful to adapt your communication style to your audience?
r: It helps the message be understood and accepted
Different people need different approaches.
w: It lets you avoid giving accurate information
Accuracy must stay the same.
It makes your message longer and more complex
Adapting often simplifies a message.
It removes the need to ask questions
Questions still help.

q: What should you do when you answer a business phone call?
r: Greet the caller, state your name and offer help
A professional greeting sets the tone.
w: Answer quickly without saying anything
The caller needs a greeting.
Ask the caller to call back later without explaining
That is not helpful.
Talk about your personal plans while waiting
That is unprofessional.

q: A team's meeting runs long because no one prepared. Which action would best improve the next meeting?
r: Share an agenda and goals beforehand
A plan keeps the meeting focused.
w: Remove time limits so everyone can talk
This could make meetings longer.
Cancel all future meetings
That removes useful coordination.
Invite more people to join without a purpose
More people can slow the meeting.

q: Which graphic aid is best for showing how a company's sales changed over twelve months?
r: A line graph
Lines show change over time.
w: A pie chart of one month's sales
A pie shows parts of a whole.
A photo of the store entrance
A photo does not show data.
A list of employee names
A list does not show sales trends.

q: What is the purpose of an executive summary?
r: To give busy readers the key points of a longer report
It helps leaders decide quickly.
w: To replace the full report completely
The report still holds the detail.
To list every employee who worked on the project
That is not its purpose.
To hide bad news from readers
A summary should be honest.

q: An employee writes 'Per my last email' in an angry tone to a coworker. What is the likely effect?
r: It may cause conflict and hurt the working relationship
Tone affects how messages are received.
w: It improves teamwork by showing strong leadership
Hostile tone rarely improves teamwork.
It makes the message more professional
It reads as irritation.
It ensures the coworker will respond faster
It may cause defensiveness instead.

q: Why should business writing use clear, simple words?
r: Readers understand it faster and with fewer errors
Clarity reduces misunderstandings.
w: Complex words always impress customers
Complexity can confuse readers.
Simple words are not allowed in formal reports
Plain language is acceptable and preferred.
Short words take more time to write
Plain language is quicker to read.

q: Which step helps you edit and revise a document effectively?
r: Review it for clarity, accuracy and errors after writing
Revising improves quality.
w: Send it immediately without reading it
Errors may remain.
Add extra words to make it longer
Length does not improve quality.
Change the topic halfway through
That would confuse the reader.

q: During a presentation, a listener asks a question you cannot answer. What is the best response?
r: Admit you do not know and offer to follow up
Honesty builds trust.
w: Make up an answer so you look prepared
False answers harm credibility.
Ignore the question and move on
Ignoring may seem disrespectful.
Tell the listener the question is not important
That is rude.

q: What is customer relationship management (CRM)?
r: Managing interactions and information to build lasting customer relationships
It tracks customer needs and history.
w: A method for lowering prices for all customers
CRM is not mainly a pricing method.
A rule that requires customers to buy monthly
CRM does not force purchases.
A way to keep customers from sharing feedback
CRM encourages feedback.

q: A customer is upset about a late delivery. What should an employee do first?
r: Listen, apologize and ask what outcome would help
This calms the customer and defines the problem.
w: Explain why the customer should have ordered earlier
That blames the customer.
Ask the customer to call back tomorrow
Delay increases frustration.
Say it is not the company's responsibility
That avoids ownership.

q: Why does a business collect customer feedback?
r: To learn what customers want and improve products and service
Feedback guides decisions.
w: To prove to customers that the company is always right
Feedback is for learning.
To reduce the number of customers served
Feedback is meant to improve service.
To avoid training employees
Feedback does not replace training.

q: A loyalty program gives a free item after ten purchases. How does this support customer relations?
r: It rewards repeat business and encourages loyalty
Rewards strengthen relationships.
w: It discourages customers from returning
Rewards encourage returns.
It reduces the quality of service
The program does not change service.
It guarantees every customer will be satisfied
It rewards loyalty, not guarantees satisfaction.

q: What does it mean to show a customer service mindset?
r: Putting customers' needs at the center of your actions
The focus is helping customers.
w: Focusing only on closing as many sales as possible
That ignores service.
Avoiding customers who ask many questions
That is the opposite.
Following only the rules that benefit the company
That ignores customer needs.

q: A customer asks for a refund outside the return window. What is the best response?
r: Explain the policy kindly and offer any allowed options
This respects policy and the customer.
w: Refuse and walk away without explaining
That is unhelpful.
Break the policy without telling a manager
Unauthorized exceptions create problems.
Argue that the customer should have read the policy
That escalates conflict.

q: How can employees build rapport with customers?
r: Greet them warmly and show genuine interest in their needs
Rapport builds trust.
w: Talk only about the company's profits
Customers care about their needs.
Avoid eye contact to seem professional
Eye contact shows attention.
Use technical terms the customer cannot follow
Jargon creates distance.

q: A company's brand promise is 'fast and friendly service.' Which employee behavior best supports it?
r: Helping each customer quickly while staying courteous
Actions should match the promise.
w: Taking long breaks during busy periods
That slows service.
Speaking sharply to customers who ask for help
That is not friendly.
Ignoring customers until they ask three times
That is not fast.

q: What is a customer touch point?
r: Any interaction a customer has with a business
Examples include websites, stores and calls.
w: A tax a customer pays on a purchase
That is a sales tax.
A coupon given only to employees
A touch point is an interaction.
A product that is out of stock
That is an inventory issue.

q: A customer says the website was confusing but the store staff were helpful. What does this show?
r: Experience can vary across touch points
Consistency across channels matters.
w: Online service is not important to customers
Many customers use websites.
Stores should close their doors
One issue does not mean closing stores.
Employees should avoid helping customers
Helpful staff are valuable.

q: Why is following up with a customer after a sale useful?
r: It shows care and can reveal problems or new needs
Follow-up supports retention.
w: It reduces the chance the customer returns
Follow-up encourages return.
It replaces the need for good products
Products still matter.
It lets the business avoid warranties
Warranties still apply.

q: Which technology helps a business keep track of customer purchase history and preferences?
r: A customer database or CRM system
It stores and organizes customer information.
w: A printer used for office documents
A printer does not track customers.
A security camera in the parking lot
That serves another purpose.
A calculator used in the back office
A calculator does not store customer data.
